title: House of Khalifa
capsule: The Al-Khalifa, of the Bani Utbah clan and Anizah tribal confederation, migrated from Najd via Kuwait and Qatar's Al Zubarah before Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Khalifa seized Bahrain from the Persian-backed Nasr Al-Madhkur in 1783. After Ahmed's death, sons Salman and Abdullah divided authority into rival Al-Salman and Al-Abdulla branches that waged open conflict between 1842 and 1846, ending in Al-Salman supremacy; the rival branch persisted until 1895. A treaty with Britain in 1861 formalized Khalifa rule in exchange for protectorate status, anchoring the dynasty against Ottoman, Wahhabi, and Persian challenges through the remainder of the 19th century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty's political history from 1783 is well documented through British India Office records and Khalifa family chronicles; precise territorial control over offshore islands in the early period is less certain.
